justification: Concurrency cap on the brief SSE stream to stop the 8GB Railway container OOM-crashing when two heavy briefs run at once (each peaks at a few GB from Sentinel-2 + pre-DA embeddings + terrain arrays). A threading.BoundedSemaphore (default 1, env BRIEF_MAX_CONCURRENCY) serialises heavy briefs; a queued request waits up to 150s then gets an honest 'busy' event instead of a crash. Investigation found the flood rasters are disk + location-gated (not the RAM cause), so lazy-loading them was NOT shipped — the concurrency cap is the actual fix.

pre_impl.existing_data: Railway logs: two POST /pipeline/intelligence-brief/stream at 07:12:06 and 07:12:19, then 'Killed' (OOM) at 07:14:08 and auto-restart. Memory is at the plan cap (8GB). Confirmed: torch is NOT imported at boot; flood_truth reads the 520MB Hawkesbury rasters only when a lot is within the study bounds (gated), so they are disk + on-demand, not a RAM baseline. The OOM is a per-brief runtime spike x concurrency.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Earlier framing blamed the 520MB rasters as RAM; investigation shows they are disk-backed (/tmp) and location-gated. The real cause is concurrent heavy briefs.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new query or pipeline. Adds a module-level BoundedSemaphore and wraps the existing _safe_brief_sse generator with acquire (timeout) / finally-release.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Independent of data sources. If the semaphore can't be acquired in time, a clean 'busy' SSE error event is emitted; the brief never crashes the container.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A (backend Python). The frontend already renders an SSE 'error' event.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a second concurrent brief could OOM-kill the container, severing all in-flight streams (and dropping the 'complete' event). After: heavy briefs serialise; a second request waits or gets an honest 'busy' message; no OOM crash.

values: N/A - no regulatory values; a concurrency constant.
queries: N/A - no database or API query.

break_it.scenario: A brief generator raises before release
break_it.what_happens: the semaphore could leak and permanently block briefs
break_it.repro: the acquire is paired with a finally: _BRIEF_SEMAPHORE.release()
break_it.how: release is in a finally so it runs on success, exception, or generator close

break_it.what_happens: the permit might not be released
break_it.repro: Python closes the generator (GeneratorExit) which runs the finally
break_it.how: the finally release runs on generator close/GC

break_it.repro: acquire has a 150s timeout; on miss it yields a 'busy' error event and returns
break_it.how: bounded wait + honest busy message, never an indefinite hang

break_it.scenario: The cap is too low and serialises legitimate concurrent demand
break_it.what_happens: legitimate users could wait too long
break_it.repro: BRIEF_MAX_CONCURRENCY is an env var; raise it once the container has more memory
break_it.how: configurable without a code change; default 1 is the safe value at 8GB

post_merge.other_repo: Railway: optionally set BRIEF_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 if you upgrade memory; leave unset (=1) on the 8GB plan. The lazy-raster idea was investigated and dropped (rasters are disk + location-gated, not the RAM cause).
post_merge.manual_verify: Fire two briefs at once: the second queues behind the first (or returns a 'busy' event) instead of OOM-killing the container; a single brief is unaffected.
